As a new player who isn't very good at the game, the only mode I can play is deathmatch because people kick me out instantly in any other mode, and I don't have any friends to play with to vote against it for me. I can't improve much because playing against bots isn't very good practice; bots behave very differently from real players. Even in deathmatch, there are tons of case-farming bot accounts that kick real players out instantly. There are also lots of people using cheats and multiple accounts, who kick players out the instant they join. Then when you get kicked out and try to join another server, you can't play at all because Valve always tries to put you in the server you just got kicked from, and then after wasting your time waiting for it to load, you get an error message saying you can't join the server. Bots, cheaters, and anyone who wants to, can literally prevent you from playing the game at all, until the server they kick you from closes. Another big issue is that there are so many toxic players in this game who will hurl slurs at you just for being inexperienced, or for no reason at all. I had to turn off the chat because of this. Reporting does nothing. Valve, as a multi-billion dollar company, you can do better. You should be investing in some decent, real human moderation instead of donating 20 million dollars to AI slop. You should be banning bots, cheaters, and those who harass and bully others. But you won't because you only care about money. The option to vote players out should be removed, especially in deathmatch. It is way too prone to abuse and prevents new players like me from getting better at the game. Some people would respond to that with "What about cheaters?". The answer is that this game wouldn't have so many cheaters if Valve actually had decent moderation. Innocent players should not be punished just because Valve has terrible moderation. At this point, I'm only playing this game to get some Steam credit from item drops, as I don't have much money, and I want to save up for some games to take my mind off of things and hopefully play with some friends someday. This game could be fun with some friends, but as an inexperienced player trying to play by myself, it's really not enjoyable.

As a player, Counter-Strike has always been an absolute legend in my eyes not just because of its pure, timeless gameplay, but because of the massive, passionate community that has kept it alive for over two decades. CS2 finally brings that legend into the Source 2 era. The visual upgrade is immediate: lighting, textures, and completely rebuilt maps like Overpass look stunning. Volumetric smoke grenades are a genuine game-changer, reshaping tactics in ways that feel fresh and strategic. The sub-tick system was meant to make actions more responsive, but the result is mixed. Shooting often feels crisp, yet movement and spraying can feel inconsistent compared to the old 128-tick servers, leading to frustrating "what you see is not what you get" moments. The weapon loadout adds personalization, but the removal of casual modes stings. Cheating has also migrated seamlessly, and Valve s anti-cheat needs significant work. Despite these issues, the core experience remains as addictive as ever. Premier mode offers structured competitive play with visible ratings. It's free-to-play, gorgeous, and the foundation is strong. CS2 is a brilliant update that still feels incomplete an 8 10 today, with every chance to become a masterpiece once Valve polishes the rough edges. Recommended.

I have been playing War Thunder since the early days, before it was on Steam, and honestly, the game is plagued with long-standing issues. For a new player, the first few tiers can be genuinely fun. The problems start once you hit certain BRs and begin moving higher in the tech trees. You might expect bigger and more tactical maps as vehicles become more advanced, but the opposite often happens: the higher you go, the smaller and more cramped the maps feel. Many top-tier ground battles end up playing more like Counter-Strike than tank combat, with constant close-quarters fights and very little room for proper positioning. The premium vehicle system feels predatory, especially toward new players. It encourages them to skip the learning process and jump straight to famous vehicles they like, such as the M1A1 Abrams, only to get thrown into high-tier matches where they are completely out of their depth. On top of that, Gaijin has recently been criticized for using AI-generated-looking content for things like skins and profile pictures, which makes the monetization feel even cheaper and more cynical. The worst thing a new player can do is buy a high-tier premium and jump straight into the grind. It is repetitive, unbalanced, and extremely punishing. You will often end up as free food for CAS, helicopters, BMPTs, and experienced players who already understand the game s mechanics. A large part of many teams is made up of people who simply do not know what is happening yet, because the game does a poor job of teaching them and encourage throwing yourself at a high tier. The lack of meaningful game modes is also a huge problem. After all these years, most battles still feel like the same team deathmatch formula. Air battles especially could be so much better with proper objectives and more varied modes, but instead they often feel like chaotic team deathmatch with far too many planes. Ground battles suffer from the same issue. The grind is another major problem. It is slow enough that the game constantly pushes you toward buying premium time and premium vehicles. But once again, if you are a new player buying your way into high tier, you are probably going to get destroyed so you won't get anywhere anytime soon. At this point, the grind speed without premium should honestly be closer to what premium accounts currently get and full premium should just x2 the progress. Ground forces in particular take far too long to progress through, while air grind feels somewhat more reasonable. Vehicle modeling and balance are also frustrating. The director is pro russian and somehow like to do taxe evasion at the same time. If you expect your favorite vehicle to be represented fairly, prepare to be disappointed. Bug reports for NATO and other non-Russian vehicles often seem to require overwhelming documentation with no room for approximation, while Russian vehicles appear to receive more generous interpretation. I do not think approximations are automatically bad, sometimes they are necessary when exact data is unavailable, but the same standard should be applied to every nation. There is also a noticeable pattern where certain mechanics or features are said to be impossible, unsuitable, or reserved for later, only for them to eventually appear in a way that benefits Russian vehicles first. This creates the impression that the game is not applying its own rules consistently. Gaijin has also destroyed a lot of player trust by constantly contradicting its own past statements. They said there would be no modern vehicles then added them. They said there would be no modern premiums then added those too. At this point, many of their promises feel meaningless. And when it comes to approximations in vehicle modeling, this is not some conspiracy invented by players. Gaijin themselves have admitted that they use approximations when exact data is missing. The issue is that this flexibility seems to appear far more often for Russian vehicles, while NATO and other nations are held to a much harsher standard where even strong sources are dismissed for not being perfect. Many other shenanigans I can't fit here. In the end, War Thunder could be massively improved with bigger maps, more varied game modes, proper team-based objectives, fewer players per match, some kind of player rating system with a low bias just to get slightly more balanced games and maybe pair the noobs together, and a more consistent standards for vehicle modeling across every nation, not less Russian bias but a more equal treatment for everyone else. Ah yes, and NO AI.

Weekends are full of hackers: The most toxic cheaters are the ones trying to pass themselves off as "god-tier" players. They use toggleable hacks to give themselves a slight edge, making it incredibly hard to prove without video review. Be warn developers don't care 1 2 Permanent Speed Boosts: A standard Killer moves slightly faster than a running survivor. Subtle cheaters give themselves a tiny 2 Haste boost. It is just enough that a Killer can follow them around a loop perfectly but never actually close the distance for a hit, making the Killer look like they just have bad pathing. Wallhacks Permanent Aura Reading: Survivors who always know exactly which way the Killer is mind-gaming behind a tall wall, or Killers who walk straight to a hidden survivor across the map without a single tracking perk. Perfect Instant Vaults: Getting a "fast vault" distance boost from an angle or speed that should have triggered a slow medium vault Auto-Aim Perfect Hitbox Registration Ever thrown a pallet directly into a Killer's face, watched them get visually stunned, but somehow their weapon still teleported through the wood to down you? How to spot it: Some software utilizes a packet-manipulation script that tells the server the Killer swung a millisecond earlier than they actually did on your screen. It forces "hit validation" in the Killer's favor, meaning they will hit you through medium vaults and dropped pallets that a regular connection or clean player would absolutely miss. To save precious seconds during a match, killers will subtly tweak their animation cooldowns by 5 to 10 . How to spot it: Watch how fast they break a pallet, wipe the blood off their weapon after a hit, or pick a survivor up off the ground. Experienced players know the exact rhythmic timing of a weapon recovery animation. If a Killer finishes their hit-recovery animation just a split-second too fast allowing them to body-block a window you should have easily made they are adjusting their recovery values. Some third-party tools don't even alter the gameplay directly they pull data from the server during the loading screen. How to spot it: The Killer can see exactly what perks, items, and offerings all four survivors have equipped before the match even starts. If you change your build to a niche perk like Calm Spirit, and suddenly you're facing a Doctor who perfectly plays around it, or you bring a Sabotage build and the Killer instantly switches to Agitation and Iron Grasp without seeing a single toolbox in the lobby, they likely sniped your loadout to counter-pick you.

Been playing this for way too long and given it too many chances (more hours than what steam says). It's the 10th anniversary and it feels like almost nothing much has improved. From terrible map designs, powercreep killers, unbalanced bloat of perks, etc. The devs seem to have no faith in this game and instead rely totally on pure addiction from their playerbase with overpriced skins and empty promises. Progression feels unrewarding and caters around the meta too heavily in terms of perk choices, killer picks and maps. There are a few creative perks in the game but it is so rare to encounter any killers or survivors running them since most of the time it will generally be the same set of perks that have not changed much at all. Even with 309 perks currently in the game, you probably will only see the same perk types being used by most players. Certain perks can cause matches to become unfun and worst case scenario make you second guess yourself since it can very hard to tell whether someone is cheating or not. Killer designs over the years have gotten increasingly uncreative and poorly designed. You can compare most killers released over the past 3 years to older killers and can tell easily how similar they are. The Animatronic Dredge Huntress. The Slasher Dredge Huntress. It's fine for people to be hyped over Jason being added, but its almost ignored and they end up getting the same killer they already had which almost makes it just a new skin for a killer that exists in DBD. The balancing of the killers is absolutely atrocious. Nurse hasn't been fixed in so long you can't even tell you're playing a match of DBD because the gameplay is non-existent, if the Nurse player understands how the power works of which people tend to overexaggerate how hard it is to learn The Nurse. Then you have the opposite, being The Trapper who is probably the saddest icon for DBD since the devs have given him zero respect and no changes for a very long time(maybe some add on changes but he sucks regardless). Also, some killer designs allow for the most boring experience you could have playing this(Nurse included) and there are too many of them. If you want to play against a killer that is interactive then that is a harsh gamble especially considering how people tend to play them. Dead by Daylight is one of those games that can be incredibly fun and frustrating in the very same match. Its core concept is still very strong: four survivors try to repair generators and escape, while a killer controlled by another player hunts them down. The idea is simple, but the amount of decisions, perks, maps, killers, playstyles, and possible situations makes every match feel different. The best part of the game is found in those tense moments: when you are being chased, when you manage to save a teammate at the last second, when you hide your tracks, when the killer barely misses a hit, or when a match that seemed completely lost ends in an escape. As a survivor, the game becomes much more enjoyable once you understand that it is not always about escaping. Sometimes it is about contributing: repairing generators, rescuing teammates, lasting long enough in a chase, buying time, or simply making a memorable play. The game also has a lot of variety in characters and builds. You can play in a more cooperative, stealthy, aggressive, altruistic, or casual way. You do not always need to use the most meta perks to have fun, and that is something I really appreciate. The perk system allows for a lot of experimentation, although it can feel overwhelming if you are coming back after a long break or if you are trying to unlock specific abilities. That being said, the game is far from perfect. The balance can be inconsistent, some matches feel unfair, matchmaking is not always great, and the community can be pretty intense. There are games where the killer dominates too quickly, others where coordinated survivors make the killer feel helpless, and others where you depend too much on random teammates. On top of that, the grind to unlock perks and prestige characters can feel heavy, especially if you want to try many different builds. The monetization is also debatable. There is a lot of unlockable content, skins, licensed characters, and DLCs. You do not need to buy everything to enjoy the game, but it is obvious that the experience becomes more appealing when you have more characters available. Still, with patience, you can unlock several original characters using the in-game currency. Visually and sonically, the game fits its identity very well. It may not feel like pure horror after many hours, because you eventually get used to it, but it still keeps a tense atmosphere. Sound is extremely important: footsteps, breathing, generators, the terror radius, screams, and killer effects all matter. When the game works well, it creates moments that very few asymmetrical multiplayer games can replicate. My biggest recommendation is not to play Dead by Daylight expecting a perfectly balanced or relaxing experience. It is chaotic, competitive, sometimes unfair, but also very addictive and unique. It becomes much more enjoyable if you play with the mindset of learning, trying different builds, and accepting that not every match will go well. In short: Dead by Daylight has many flaws, but its formula is just too entertaining. It can frustrate you, hook you, make you close the game angry, and then make you open it again the next day. If you enjoy asymmetrical multiplayer games, tense chases, and the feeling of slowly improving, it is absolutely worth playing. I recommend it, especially if you play with friends or enjoy experimenting with different playstyles.

Counterstrike is a mecanically difficult game but once you see how good or great players play you will understand step by step and how to generally understand what's happening in the many rounds you will have and how to make the best decisions for you and your teammates. The Pro scene is also incredible to watch and entertaining, to see how incredible players play and how they understand the game and apply their strategies, the decisions they make, some have a flashy style some have a more passive style but its fun and great to see and watch masters in their domain. I also like how simple yet difficult the game is, there is no drones, no special powers but you need good mecanical skills and coordination with your team (that many times fails) in order to improve and win rounds. The way they interact with bullets and explosions completely changes the tactical depth. Cons: Cheaters are honestly everywhere right now, and it can get incredibly frustrating to deal with them so often. The matchmaking sometimes feels completely unbalanced, putting you into matches that feel entirely one-sided. With the launch of Premier Mode, Valve aimed to bring the professional tournament experience directly to the casual and hardcore player alike, reducing the community's reliance on third-party platforms like FACEIT. The Pick Ban Phase Premier Mode introduces a sleek veto system where teams take turns banning maps until a single battleground is left. This forces players to expand their map pool rather than just grinding Mirage or Dust II all day. The CS Rating Leaderboards Instead of the classic hidden Elo ranks (Silver, Gold Nova, Global Elite), Premier utilizes a transparent numerical CS Rating (e.g., 12,500, 21,000) paired with regional and global leaderboards. The Good: You know exactly how many points you stand to win or lose before the match even starts. The Bad: The classic competitive mode still exists but tracks ranks individually per map, which fractured the player base and made traditional ranks feel less prestigious.

Lag. Terrible rubber banding even though I'm hardwired, 24 ping, and never experience this kind of connectivity issue in other games except ones that are well known to have networking issues. The number of times I see someone shoot and they completely miss the other player but still hit is unbelievable. I played 10's of thousands of hours of 1.6 and never had such bad issues even on 56k. Where you shot was where the bullet went and it was incredibly rare to see object placement discrepancies due to ping - and when you did see them, it was far less egregious. The crosshair bounces all over the place making it highly difficult to place follow up shots quickly or manage the recoil pattern as the screen shakes preventing reliable prediction. Follow recoil, don't follow recoil, they're both pretty terrible to play with. Especially against people who have played with it for thousands of hours and are used to it. Some people would call it a skill gap - I would call it making the game harder to play than necessary. Weapon balancing is awful. The m4a1 has a 20 round clip? I thought the trade off on silence was the dink with armor vs. the ak 1 shot. The negev is way too accurate over range. The auto shotgun has the same problem. I've seen way too many across a bombsite headshot kills in 1-2 shots with it. It's like there is no real spread and you're shooting slugs...but your not. Tech9 is way op too...i've seen 1 shot headshots up close with it, the fire rate is way to high and the recoil far too little. It's way better than pretty much any other pistol because of how easy it is to use. Only the deagle (maybe r8 but why is there an r8?) beats it over range...and the deagle (along with plenty of other guns) have a strange bullet spread over distance that make them unwieldly. Though this might be due to the lag issue mentioned above. Quite frankly, I don't know why they added so many more weapons and changed the standing weapon characteristics when the balancing was pretty much perfect in 1.6. I also don't know how the internet has gotten better but this game has gotten worse. On top of these core issues that are impossible to fix at this point (I would guess since they haven't been in the case of lag - and it's not like they can change weapons since it would mess with the skin market) there are things they can fix but don't. 1 - Match results screen is not skippable. This means most times you don't get to vote on the next map. God forbid you level up prime and then you never see the vote screen. To think I paid extra money for this feature is ridiculous. 2 - There are a large number of maps missing from the original game, leaving the map pool quite small. Estate, prodigy, assault, aztec, dust, cbble are all missing. I'm also missing at least 2 that I can't remember off the top of my head what they're names were. 3 - There is a serious lack of game modes. Free for all deathmatch is the only one? Why not team? IMO match making killed what helped make CS great to begin with. 4 - Plan to spend at least 1000 dollars if you want to pull your own knife. I've spent about 250 and only ever gotten 1 pink - wait, is black lotus pink? Forget about red and golds I guess huh? I've watched peanut pull probably over 1k of cases and he has similar luck - though he just got a knife for the first time not in trade up. And I haven't watched him play that much CS either. You're just better off buying a skin if you want something which is what I ended up doing for a fraction of the cost. IDK how there are so many kids playing this game since gambling is such a core part of it's ecosystem. It's such a terrible experience too, but then again I don't like to gamble. 5 - Speaking of kids, the community (due to match making and not server based anymore) is toxic. The number of people abusing others, calling them slurs, targeting women and just being bad people in general is crazy.

After spending many hours playing Premier in Counter-Strike 2, I can say it's the best competitive mode in the game. The CS Rating system is also motivating, giving you a clear sense of progression and something to work toward every match. Of course, it's not perfect. Matchmaking can sometimes feel unbalanced, with players of different skill levels ending up in the same game. There are also occasional issues with toxic teammates and suspected cheaters. However, when both teams are evenly matched, the matches are intense, rewarding, and incredibly fun. Overall, Premier offers the most authentic competitive Counter-Strike experience available in CS2.
